content_units: Seasonal Allergy Relief Overview
This pattern is most consistent with   mild allergic rhinitis/conjunctivitis  : sneezing, itchy eyes, and runny nose without fever, breathing trouble, or facial pain.
Context for this guidance
- Adult, age   34
- Symptoms for   6 days
- No regular medicines reported
-   Penicillin allergy does not affect typical OTC allergy medicines
Over-the-Counter Options
Option   What it helps most   Common examples   Common side effects   Notes

Non-drowsy oral antihistamine   Sneezing, itching, runny nose   cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine   sleepiness possible (more with cetirizine), dry mouth, headache   Good simple first option for daytime symptoms
Antihistamine eye drops   Itchy/watery eyes   ketotifen, olopatadine   brief stinging, dryness, mild irritation   Often works better for eyes than oral tablets

Steroid nasal spray   Nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose   fluticasone, triamcinolone, budesonide   nose irritation, dryness, minor nosebleeds   Usually the most effective overall nasal treatment; may take a few days for full effect

Saline nasal spray/rinse   Nasal irritation, mucus, allergen washout   sterile saline spray or rinse   mild discomfort, ear fullness if used incorrectly   Drug-free and can be combined with other options

Decongestant   Stuffy nose only   pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine   jitteriness, fast heartbeat, insomnia, raised blood pressure   Best for short-term use; avoid if he has high BP, heart rhythm issues, or significant anxiety
Practical take
- For   sneezing + itchy eyes + runny nose  , a   non-drowsy oral antihistamine   is a common starting choice.
- If nasal symptoms are the main issue, a   steroid nasal spray   is often the most effective OTC option.
- If the eyes are especially bothersome, add   antihistamine eye drops  .
- Avoid combining multiple products with overlapping ingredients unless the label clearly supports it.
Non-Drug Relief Measures
Option 1: Pollen reduction routine   Lower exposure can meaningfully reduce symptoms   Best for outdoor-triggered allergies
- Shower and change clothes after time outdoors
- Keep windows closed during high-pollen periods
- Use air conditioning or a clean HEPA-style room filter if available
Pollen Tips
Option 2: Saline rinse   Helps wash out pollen and mucus from the nose   Drug-free support
- Use sterile/distilled/previously boiled water only
- Can be done once or twice daily during symptom flares
- Useful before a nasal spray
Safe Rinsing
Option 3: Eye comfort measures   Best for itchy, irritated eyes   Simple symptom relief
- Try cool compresses over closed eyes
- Use preservative-free artificial tears to flush allergens
- Avoid rubbing the eyes
When Medical Care Would Be a Good Idea
Seek medical advice if any of these happen:
- Symptoms last   more than 2-4 weeks   or keep recurring and are hard to control
- Symptoms become   moderate to severe   or disrupt sleep/work
- He develops   wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness  , or coughing fits
- He gets   fever, facial pain/pressure, thick one-sided nasal discharge  , or worsening sinus pain
- There is a   rash, swelling  , or a reaction after taking a medicine
- Frequent nosebleeds or significant irritation from nasal sprays
- Eye symptoms become   painful  , light-sensitive, or affect vision
